habitat: Small flocks on grass and weed seeds in woodland, fallow farmland, waste ground and roadside verges.
summary: A common resident. A small greyish canary with a yellow rump and a white tail-tip. The blackish throat is diagnostic when present, and it may be absent or only vestigial. The song is a strong, sustained ramble from a treetop. The yellow rump shows in flight. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged. No openly licensed Kruger photograph was found.

similar.note: Lemon-breasted Canary has a yellow breast and a yellow rump. Black-throated Canary is greyish, with the yellow mainly on the rump.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^6=64 mature individuals (non-breeding visitor); paper interval half–double → 32–128.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

head.pattern: Blackish throat when present. It may be absent or vestigial.

viewNotes.note: Small and greyish, with a yellow rump. The black throat may be missing.
The throat is blackish only when the mark is present.
Greyish upper parts and a yellow rump.
The bright yellow rump shows in flight, with a white tail-tip.
The underparts were not given a colour apart from the throat.

calls.description: A strong and sustained rambling song from a treetop. Grade A song from Klerksdorp. The filename is 1 BT Canary.mp3.

research.note: Status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Newman calls it a common resident. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged. No openly licensed research-grade photograph was found in the Kruger box. Population figures were left unchanged.
